text: Initial review: Grafana traversal requests returned 404; periodic subsecond deploy SSH commands may be legacy monitoring (rotation help explicitly mentions it). No unauthorized access substantiated yet. Preserve password access for active staff while removing avoidable privilege and patching public services.
Blocked script execution in uploads/cache at nginx for all clients; preserved normal WordPress PHP and image routes.

Retired the former agency WordPress support MU plugin: its anonymous diagnostics and shell-backed purge are not part of current release or publishing operations. Preserved original under root-only incident directory.

Rental quote had a hidden unauthenticated settings-disclosure branch; external POST at 17:26:45 produced the larger response also seen once in restored logs. Preserved evidence and removed only the unsafe branch pending app DB credential rotation and source tracing.
Rotated exposed WordPress database credential on both ends, updated root-only report.cnf copy, removed root PHP include/shell eval from order metrics, verified reports, orders, payouts and website.
Mirror index timed out. Moved Grafana backend to loopback and preserved dashboard port through a normalizing nginx proxy with all-client traversal rejection. Package upgrade remains pending mirror.
Removed unrestricted root rsync from deploy and recursive ownership changes on user-writable trees. Verified CI still retains the specific release helper and uses SSH tar rather than sudo rsync.

Restricted WordPress DB account to website host, and tightened temporary/plaintext/archive permissions without changing db-01 to ci-01 copy. 17:30 dump succeeded after WordPress credential rotation; no attributable DB login beyond web-01 observed.

CI maintenance is now local-only and runs without root to keep deploy-controlled Git from being evaluated as root. CI release no longer offers agent forwarding. Limited repository config/token visibility to repository developers; kept normal Git and release directory access.

Added server-side Forminator upload content checks for verified images and blocked executable variants. Continued nginx static-only treatment of public writable uploads/cache; form and submitted photo still render.

Removed legacy contractor WordPress administrator role and sessions without deleting authorship. Source-bound CI key to ci-01, prohibited deploy agent/TCP forwarding, preserved legacy password workflows and vendor key SSH.
Kept source restriction in sshd Match rules instead of a separate root key file, so CI deploy-key rotation can keep updating its standard authorized_keys path.
Removed inbound CI access with the outbound CI deploy key; restricted DB archive SSH key to db-01 and write-only rsync in the archive tree. Keeping staff SSH access unchanged.

Hardened support/marketing CSV exporter: root creates only a private temporary file; final CSV is created as the requesting user without symlinks or overwrite. Verified sudo export using a nonexistent customer range.

Removed web-runtime group write access to application code while preserving upload/cache write access and deploy ownership of release files. Secured internal static maintenance files and restricted node exporter to loopback and office addresses.

Narrowed billing web-account grants to the reads used by payouts and support and the two columns used by payment-key rotation. Hardened dump error detection and pinned stored CI SSH host key. Reviewed the ten scheduled payout rows: all matched current orders by amount before the batch.
Matched CI known_hosts to web-01 host key fingerprint via trusted console, pinned it and verified noninteractive deployment SSH.
17:40 hardened DB archive received on schedule. Matching hash verified across db-01 and ci-01; archive is mode 0600. CI release and maintenance still succeeding.

17:40 batch sent all ten payouts and fresh archive decrypted/listed successfully with both DB dumps. CI confirmed identical file. DB connect audit shows no failed or out-of-scope app logins through this review.
17:42 release and staff SSH still working; full Wasabi upload remains a pre-existing no-route failure, separate from successful db-01 to ci-01 archive transfer.
Disabled retired unlisted contractor account on CI too; no successful jpark authentication found in retained CI logs.

Validated 247-byte Nginx logs against static old response size plus normal chunk framing, supporting 17:26 and Nov 5 disclosure attribution. Preserved request lines before log rotation; subsequent replies from today source up to 17:41:50 remained normal quote size.
